sample_unit: hours of speech data (robot-patient and doctor-patient dialogues)

links.outcome: LLM confidence calibration when selecting sentences in medical dialogues
links.effect: All three LLMs were highly overconfident in probabilistic predictions whether correct or incorrect; best accuracy was Claude Sonnet 4 at 71.1% (manual transcripts) and 74.7% (automatic transcripts).
links.quote: Experimental results reveal that Claude Sonnet 4 is the best in sentence selection, with 71.1% accuracy using manual transcriptions and 74.7% using automatic transcriptions, and that all LLMs are highly overconfident in their probabilistic predictions, regardless of selecting correct or incorrect sentences in medical dialogues.

screen.reason: The paper introduces a dataset (MeDial-Speech) of medical dialogues and benchmarks several LLMs on a sentence selection task, also reporting on model overconfidence.
